modifiedBy.description: The identifier of the user who last modified the block.

parentId.description: The identifier of the parent block; empty for root blocks.

schema.description: The schema version of the block.

type.description:

properties.description: Free-form properties of the board itself.

showDescription.description: Whether the description is shown in the interface.

templateVersion.description: The version of the built-in template this board came from.

title.description:

type.description: Whether the board is open or private.

updateAt.description: Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

workspaceId.description: The identifier of the workspace the board belongs to.

oneOf.description: The highest role inherited from teams; direct flags remain unchanged.

blocks.description: The blocks; each must belong to one of `boards`.

Card.description: A card: a titled group of properties with a body on a board.

boardId.description: The identifier of the board the card belongs to.

oneOf.description:
The card's body. `null` for a card without one, and in a list of cards, which
says only whether there is one (`hasBody`): a card is read alone for its body.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

createdBy.description: The identifier of the user who created the card.

deleteAt.description: Deletion time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero if not deleted.

hasBody.description: Whether the card has a body.

icon.description: The card's icon; at most one grapheme.

isTemplate.description: Whether the card is a template.

lastCommentAt.description:
When the card's last comment was posted (the `createAt` of the newest of its
comments, the blocks of the type `comment` directly on it), in milliseconds since
the Unix epoch; zero if it has none. Changing a comment does not change it; a
deleted comment does not count, and counts again with its time if restored. A
comment does not change the card's `updateAt`. A new comment comes as
`UPDATE_BLOCK`, so a client can keep the newer time; after a deletion the card is
read again for it. A number sent here in a request is ignored.

modifiedBy.description: The identifier of the user who last modified the card.

oneOf.description:
What a gallery shows of the card's body: only in a list asked for it
(`getCards` with `preview=true`), and left out otherwise. A request need not send
it; what it sends is not stored.

properties.description:
Property values keyed by property identifier: a string, a list of strings, or
`null`, and for a property of the type `date` a date value (`{"from":
"2026-03-05"}`, `{"from": "2026-03-05", "to": "2026-03-09"}` or `{"from":
1772703000000}`) or `null`.

tasksDone.description: How many task items of the body are checked.

tasksTotal.description: How many task items the body has.

updateAt.description: Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

CardPatch.description: What a card is changed to. A member that is left out stays as it is.

oneOf.description: The new body; `null` takes the body away. Sent only with `readAt`.

deletedProperties.description:
Identifiers of properties whose value the card is to lose. A property named here
and in `updatedProperties` loses its value.

icon.description: The new icon; at most one grapheme.

readAt.description:
The `updateAt` of the card as the client read it: if the card has changed since,
the patch is refused with 409 and changes nothing. Needed with `body`, and
checked whenever it is sent.

updatedProperties.description:
Property values to set, by property identifier, each replacing the card's value
for that property. The card's other values stay as they are: two patches that
set different properties of a card at about the same time both keep theirs, and
of two that set the same property the later one wins.

CardPreview.description: What a gallery shows of a card's body.

imageFileId.description:
The file the body's first image shows (`getFile` gives it, and `getSharedFile` to
the holder of the board's link); empty if the body has no image.

text.description:
The beginning of the body's text: its plain text as it is searched (a line per
paragraph, heading, code block and formula block, separated by `\n`; a formula
gives its source, an image and a mention nothing), at most 200 UTF-16 code units,
cut between characters as they are seen (a flag or a letter with its accent stays
whole), without white space at its end. Nothing says it was cut. Empty for a card
without text.

teammateNameDisplay.description: How other users' names are displayed.

version.description:
The place of the version among the comment's, counted from 1 for the text it was

writtenBy.description:
Who wrote this version: the author of the comment for the first one, and for
each later one who changed the body to it.

it back (`undeleteBlock`, `undeleteBoard`).

does not.

extension.description: The lower-cased extension of the name, with its leading dot.

Problem.description:
The JSON body the server sends with every error status of the API, as
`application/problem+json` (RFC 9457).

A client decides by `status` and, where there is one, `reason`; both are stable,
and so is `type`. `title` and `detail` are English text for logs and developers.

detail.description:
What went wrong this time, in English. Not for showing to users, and without
internals.

`changePassword`, `patchMe`, `patchUserSettings`, `patchClientState`,
`createSubscription`, `createUpload`, `createImportUpload`, `setSharing`,
`getCards`, `createCard` and `patchCard` list everything their check of the
request's own shape refuses, the first 100; so does the check of a category's
own members. Every other refusal names the one thing it is about: what is only
known from what is stored, a block of a request with several, and the first
node of a document (`body`) that may not be stored.

orgId.description:
The organization whose provider the session must be made through, with the
reason `sso_required`: what the sign-in is started for.

info.description:
The API of an fvoci server.

## Signing in

`login` answers with a `Set-Cookie` header that carries the session: the cookie `__Host-fvoci_session` where the server is reached over HTTPS, `fvoci_session` over plain HTTP. It is `HttpOnly`, so a page's scripts never see it, and a browser sends it by itself. A client that is no browser may send the cookie's value as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` instead. The operations under `/shared/{boardId}` need no session: they read a shared board with its `readToken`, and look at no session that comes along.

## Requests that change something

Every request whose method is not `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` needs the header `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`, unless it has a bearer token, and is refused with 403 and the reason `csrf` without it. If it has an `Origin` header, the origin must be the server's own (or one the server was configured to accept); otherwise it is refused with 403 and the reason `foreign_origin`.

A page should make these requests with `fetch` in its default mode, `cors`. The server sends its pages with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and under that policy a browser writes `Origin: null` on a changing request of any other mode (`same-origin`, `no-cors`, or a form the browser posts itself), which is refused as a foreign origin.

## Answers

An operation answers 200 with a body, 201 with what it made, or 204 with no body. Every other status comes with a `Problem`, the problem details of RFC 9457, as `application/problem+json`: `type` names the kind of the problem and is the same for every problem of the kind, `title` is its name, `status` repeats the status and `detail` says what went wrong this time. `type` is `/problems/<name>` under the path the server is served at, the address of a page of text about the kind; `/problems` lists them, and so does `x-problem-types` of the schema `Problem`, as they are on a server at the root of its host (a server under a path has that path before each). `reason` tells apart causes a client must tell apart; a problem with a `reason` has the `type` of that name, written with hyphens, and any other the `type` of its status. `errors` lists what of the request was refused, each by a JSON Pointer into the body (`pointer`), the name of a parameter of the query or the path (`parameter`), or the name of a header (`header`). `limit` is the limit that was exceeded: bytes for a body that was too large (413), a count for too many of something. `instance` is the request, `urn:uuid:` and its `requestId`. A session that is missing or over is 401. What the user may not see is 404, as if it were not there; what they may see but not do is 403. A path that is no operation is 404 too, and a method an operation's path does not have is 405.

A request without a session whose JSON body has more than 64 KiB is 413 before it is 401.

The identifiers of users, workspaces, boards, blocks and categories are UUIDs, written lower-case with hyphens; a client takes every identifier as an opaque string. A `fileId` is no UUID: it is an unguessable name that ends in the file's extension. Times are milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

## Lists

Every list comes in an order, and the description of each operation says which. Where it says nothing else, the order is that of creation, oldest first, and by identifier among what was created in the same millisecond.

## Bodies edited together

While people edit a card's body together the server holds it as a Y document. What it refuses of an editor has the reason `update_refused`, `update_out_of_step`, `update_too_large` or `document_too_large`; `too_many_documents` and `document_unavailable` say that it cannot take the document for now. A write of a card's whole body here (a patch of the card or of blocks, a card stored again) first writes to the card what its editors typed: a `readAt` from before that is refused with 409, and if it cannot be written the write is refused with `document_unavailable`. The editors themselves speak to the server over the websocket, whose messages name the same reasons (`contracts/websocket.md`); `document_read_only`, `connection_too_slow`, `too_many_documents_joined`, `document_full`, `too_many_connections_joined` and `too_many_frames` come only there. The page of each kind says when it comes.

## Request bodies

A request schema lists the members a request is for. An optional member may be left out or be `null`. A member the schema marks as required is one the request cannot do without; where the server takes a missing one as empty instead of refusing the request, the result is that of the empty value (a login without a password is a failed login). A body with members the schema does not list is mostly not refused for them. The exceptions: `patchUserSettings` and `patchMe` refuse every member they do not know, `createBoard` and `createCategory` refuse an `id`, and `setSharing` refuses a `token`.

get.description:
Where a provider sends the browser back to: each organization has an address of its
own, its provider's `redirectUri`, and a sign-in started for one organization does
not finish at another's address, nor with an `iss` (RFC 9207) other than the
provider's, before any code is exchanged. The sign-in is taken by its `state`, once, and only from the
browser that started it; another browser takes nothing. The code is
exchanged for an ID token, whose signature, issuer, audience, time and nonce are
checked. The person is known by the issuer and the subject: an account of theirs
signs in, and somebody who has none gets one, if the organization lets newcomers in
and no account has their email address. The session comes in the `Set-Cookie`
header, and the browser goes to the web app (303). A sign-in that was started to
link sets no session: the browser goes to the web app with `oidc_linked=1` in the
query.

Otherwise the browser goes to the login page of the organization (`/login?org=…`),
with the reason of what went wrong in `oidc_error`, by the name of its problem
(`oidc_state_invalid` as `oidc-state-invalid`): `oidc_state_invalid`, `oidc_denied`,
`oidc_token_refused`, `oidc_token_invalid`, `oidc_email_missing`,
`oidc_email_unverified`, `oidc_email_taken`, `oidc_join_closed`,
`oidc_identity_taken`, `oidc_email_mismatch` or `oidc_unavailable`.

post.description:
For the login page of the server, as a request of its own, not an address a browser
is sent to: like every request that changes something it needs the header
`X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` and no foreign `Origin`, which a page of another
site cannot send, so that no such page can sign a browser in to an account of its
choosing. Starts a sign-in for the organization `org` and answers where the page
sends the browser (the provider), with a cookie that ties the sign-in to this
browser, and ten minutes to come back. 409 with the reason `oidc_unavailable` if
the organization has no provider that is on, or it cannot be reached; 429 when
this address made too many sign-ins of late.

With `linkPassword` in the body the sign-in links: it needs the session of the
browser's cookie (401 without; a bearer token does not do, as the browser comes back
with its cookie), whose account's password that is, and when the browser comes back, who the provider
vouches for is tied to that account in place of signing in (`getMyIdentities`);
after that the provider signs in to the account. No account is made and none is
joined to another: an identity that is another account's is refused
(`oidc_identity_taken`), and so is one whose email address, as the provider has
checked it, is not the account's own (`oidc_email_mismatch`): the password ties no
other person of the provider to the account. It ends only in the browser that started it and still has
the session it was started from (`oidc_state_invalid` otherwise). A wrong password
is 400 with the reason `invalid_credentials`, naming `/linkPassword`, counted as a
wrong one of `changePassword` is; an account without a password is 409 with the
reason `password_not_set`. The session need not open the organization. A body with
another member, or a `linkPassword` that is no text, is 400 naming it: what was
meant to link does not sign in instead.

post.description:
Lets somebody into the workspace the link of `token` leads into, and answers where
that is. A request with a session lets in the user of the session, and names no
`account` (400 if it does). A request without one makes the `account` it names and
lets that in: the account's members are checked as `register` checks them (400,
with `errors`, which name them under `/account`), and a name or an email address
that is taken is 409 with the reason `username_taken` or `email_taken`. Accepting
does not sign in.

A member's link makes the account a member of the workspace and of its
organization; who is a guest of the workspace becomes a member, and who works there
already stays what they are. A guest's link puts the account on its board, in the
link's role or the higher one the account has there: who is no member of the
workspace becomes a guest of it (and no member of its organization), and who is one
stays what they are in it. The answer names the board then (`boardId`). The account
is made, the membership stored and the use of the link counted together or not at
all, and an acceptance that changes nothing uses nothing of the link.

A session that the link's organization does not take (it takes no password,
`ssoRequired`, and the session was not made through its provider) is 401 with the
reason `sso_required` and its `orgId`, and lets nobody in.

A token that lets nobody in is 404 with the reason `invitation_unavailable`,
whatever is wrong with it: there is no such link, it ended, it was used as often as
it may be, it was revoked, or who made it may no longer invite. Requests are counted
by where they come from, and too many are 429.

put.description:
Sets the organization's `OpenID Connect` provider, in place of the one it has. The
discovery document of an issuer that is not the organization's already is read
first: it must name the issuer exactly and have
`https` endpoints, or the request is 400 with the reason `oidc_issuer_unverified`
and `errors` naming `/issuer`. The server reaches only `https` addresses, follows no
redirect, and reaches only public addresses unless its configuration lets it
(`oidc_allow_private_addresses`).

`clientSecret` left out keeps the stored secret while the issuer and the client stay
the same; with another issuer or client it is required when a secret is stored (400,
`required` at `/clientSecret`), as the secret is the old client's. The empty string
stores none. The secret is stored sealed with the server's key and never answered:
without the key the request is 409 with the reason `secret_key_required`. `autoJoin`
and `enabled` left out stay as they are, also for another issuer or client, and are
on when the organization has no provider.

`ssoRequired` true makes the organization take no password: from the next request
on, what is the organization's (the routes under `/w/{workspaceId}` and
`/org/{orgId}`, and `getMyMemberships` and `setUserAdmin` where the organization is
the one the server stands in) answers 401 with the reason `sso_required` to every
session that was not made through this provider, and the websocket follows none of
its workspaces for one. The
sessions stay, and open what is of other organizations. It is switched on by a
session that was itself made through this provider, switched on, or the request is
409 with the reason `sso_unproven`: who asks has then shown that it lets them in.
While it is on, the provider is not switched off (`enabled` false), not set to
another issuer or client, and not removed: 409 with the reason `sso_enforced`,
unless the same request switches `ssoRequired` off. Left out it stays as it is,
and is off when the organization has no provider. A provider changed by another request
since this one read it is 409, to be read and sent again. The answer's `redirectUri`
is the address to register with the provider, exactly: the organization's own,
`…/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback/{orgId}`, the same before the provider is set and after
it is changed.
